# feat(moe): logical token multiplicities and fixed-row router blocks

## What this PR does

In a packed layout one row can stand for several logical tokens. For example,
a shared prompt row stands for one copy of the prompt per completion. This PR
lets the MoE router count such rows correctly for expert-bias updates and makes
its forward routing scores independent of packing. Only
`local_tokens_per_expert` is weighted. Aux losses, z-loss, capacity dropping,
quantile balancing, routing replay and router diagnostics still count physical
rows, and the backward GEMMs are unchanged, so a caller must disable those
features. #7914 rejects the loss, dropping, balancing and replay settings; router
diagnostics must be left off by the caller. Without a caller that opts in, routing is
unchanged.

## Changes

- `token_multiplicities` (optional, default `None`) on `TopKRouter.forward`,
  `InferenceTopKRouter.forward`, `TopKRouter.routing`,
  `TopKRouter._apply_expert_bias` and `MoELayer.route`. When set, each row is
  counted that many times in `local_tokens_per_expert`, so expert-bias updates
  match a dense forward. Counts stay exact in the existing int64 buffer.
  - On the default path, routers and routing callables are still called with
    exactly the upstream keywords.
  - Existing callers and replacement `routing` callables therefore keep
    working.
- `RouterInterface.forward` declares the optional argument, and the router
  docstrings describe it: one logical token count per flattened
  sequence-first row.
- `shared_prefix_token_multiplicities`: a keyword-only argument of
  `MoELayer.forward`, `None` by default. It holds one logical token count per
  flattened sequence-first row of `hidden_states`.
  - `MoELayer.forward` hands it to `route()` as `token_multiplicities`,
    including on the megakernel path.
  - The MoE recompute and megakernel checkpoints capture it in the closure they
    recompute, so a backward replay counts with the same values.
  - Paths that call `route()` directly or replay a CUDA graph do not receive
    it, so a caller must use the eager forward.
  - The MoE layer keeps no per-call state.
- `TransformerLayer` passes `shared_prefix_token_multiplicities` to the MoE
  layer only.
  - `TransformerLayer.forward` removes it from its keyword arguments before
    `_forward_attention`, so attention never sees it.
  - `_forward_mlp` and `_run_mlp` pass it on to the MLP, and
    `MoETransformerLayer._forward_mlp` passes it on to the eager path.
  - When `_run_mlp` runs the MLP in sequence chunks, it splits the
    multiplicities by chunk. Each chunk owns a contiguous range of the
    flattened rows.
  - A recomputed MLP receives the value through the checkpointed call's
    arguments.
  - A non-`None` value raises `ValueError` with a dense MLP, with
    `packed_seq_params`, or with partial MoE CUDA graphs. With
    `packed_seq_params`, rows may be un-flattened and reordered before the MoE
    layer, so the counts would no longer match their rows.
  - Without the argument, `TransformerLayer` behaves as before.
- `moe_utils.router_gating_token_blocks()`: inside this scope the forward
  router GEMM runs over fixed row blocks. A packing change can otherwise select a
  different GEMM reduction, and even FP32 router differences below 2e-6 can
  flip BF16 expert choices.
- `tensor_parallel/random.py`: `CheckpointFunction` and
  `CheckpointWithoutOutput` recompute inside a copy of the forward pass's
  `contextvars` context.
  - CUDA autograd can run backward on an engine thread with different context
    values.
  - Without this change, a forward-scoped setting such as the
    `router_gating_token_blocks()` scope is lost during recomputation.
  - Tensor observations stay suspended inside the restored context.
  - This applies to every recompute through these two helpers and keeps
    results unchanged. `te_checkpoint`, used with FP8/FP4, is unchanged.
- `RouterGatingLinearFunction.backward` computes only the gradients autograd
  requires. A frozen router still produces the input gradient but skips the
  weight-gradient GEMM, which has no consumer. This applies to every MoE run.

## Tests

```bash
# 1. one rank
python -m pytest tests/unit_tests/shared_prefix/test_router_shared_prefix.py \
    tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/test_moe_kernels.py \
    tests/unit_tests/tensor_parallel/test_random.py \
    tests/unit_tests/transformer/test_transformer_layer.py \
    tests/unit_tests/transformer/moe/test_routers.py -k "not virtual_expert"
# 2. four ranks
torchrun --nproc-per-node=4 -m pytest tests/unit_tests/shared_prefix/test_router_shared_prefix.py \
    tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/test_moe_kernels.py \
    tests/unit_tests/transformer/moe/test_moe_layer.py -k "not virtual_expert"
# 3. one rank
python -m pytest tests/unit_tests/shared_prefix/test_router_shared_prefix.py
```

All runs used one GB200 node and container rl-gym.63635108 (torch 2.11.0+cu130,
Transformer Engine 2.15.0, mamba-ssm 2.3.2.post1, causal-conv1d 1.6.2.post1,
flash-attn 2.8.1).
Commands 1 and 2 ran on f08b00003, and command 3 ran on cb6ef0f30.
cb6ef0f30 differs from f08b00003 only in `test_router_shared_prefix.py`, where
it seeds the model-parallel RNG in the four `TransformerLayer` multiplicity
tests.

- Command 1: 299 passed, 14 failed, 23 errors, 44 skipped, 23 deselected,
  2 xfailed, 1 xpassed.
  - Four failures are `test_transformer_layer_routes_multiplicities_to_moe_layer`
    `[eager]`, `[moe_recompute]` and `[chunked]`, and
    `test_transformer_layer_rejects_multiplicities_for_dense_mlp`.
    They failed because the tests did not seed the model-parallel RNG.
  - The other 33 also fail on main 90f4d5279 in the same container:
    - `test_random.py::test_model_parallel_cuda_manual_seed` and
      `test_random.py::test_checkpoint`;
    - six `test_transformer_layer.py::TestParallelTransformerLayer::test_sharded_state_dict`
      cases;
    - `test_routers.py::test_router_gating_linear[router_dtype1]` and
      `test_routers.py::test_router_gating_linear_bias[router_dtype1]`, the FP32
      Transformer Engine GEMM cases;
    - 23 errors in `test_routers.py::TestGroupLimitedRouter` and
      `test_routers.py::TestAuxLossFreeTop2Router`, whose setup requests
      expert-model-parallel size 8.
- Command 2: 187 passed, 24 failed, 18 skipped, 23 deselected, 2 xfailed,
  1 xpassed.
  - Four failures are the same `TransformerLayer` multiplicity tests, for the
    same missing seed.
  - The other 20 also fail on main 90f4d5279 in the same container: four
    `test_moe_layer.py::TestMoELayerFP16::test_moe_layer_fp16_forward_backward`
    cases and 16
    `test_moe_layer.py::TestMoELayerRecompute::test_moe_layer_recompute_forward_backward`
    cases.
- `test_moe_kernels.py` had no failures on one or four ranks.
- Command 3: 59 passed.
- Command 2 was not rerun on cb6ef0f30, so the fixed seed tests were checked
  on one rank only.

What the tests added or extended by this PR check:

- `tests/unit_tests/shared_prefix/test_router_shared_prefix.py`:
  - the routing signature without multiplicities;
  - exact logical counts;
  - `TransformerLayer` hands the multiplicities to `MoELayer.forward`, and the
    router counts each row that many times, on the eager, MoE-recompute and
    chunked-MLP paths;
  - a `TransformerLayer` with a dense MLP rejects them;
  - fixed-row blocks against per-block copies;
  - gradients for all seven combinations of trainable input, weight and bias.
    These run on the float64 `torch.mm` path; the Transformer Engine GEMM
    backward is not checked with frozen inputs.
- `tests/unit_tests/tensor_parallel/test_random.py`: the forward context is
  restored during recomputation, without duplicate tensor observations.
- `tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/test_moe_kernels.py`: bit-exact
  replays of the changed router paths.

## Shared-prefix stack

#7914 was split into the eight branches below, so that each one needs fewer
CODEOWNERS groups and can be reviewed on its own. #7914 itself keeps the
HybridModel integration. Shared-prefix execution stores a prompt once per star
(by default up to 16 completions of the same group) and runs those completions
against it, instead of repeating the prompt in every packed row.

| PR | Branch | Reviewer groups | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|
| #8152 RL packing library | `shared-prefix/p1-rl-packing` | reinforcement-learning | — |
| #8153 MoE multiplicities and recompute context | `shared-prefix/p2-moe-multiplicities` | core, mixture-of-experts, transformer | — |
| #8155 MTP loss groups | `shared-prefix/p3-mtp-loss-groups` | core, transformer | — |
| #8156 forest attention and layout | `shared-prefix/p4-forest-attention` | core, transformer | — |
| #8157 Mamba state fork | `shared-prefix/p5-mamba-state-fork` | core, hybrid-model | #8156 |
| #7914 HybridModel integration | `shared-prefix/hybrid-kernels-20261006` | core, hybrid-model | #8153, #8155, #8157 |
| #8158 RL packaging | `shared-prefix/p7-rl-packaging` | ci | #8152 |
| RL planner parity test (no PR number yet) | `shared-prefix/p8-rl-parity` | none required | #8152, #7914 |

#8152, #8153, #8155 and #8156 can merge in any order. A dependent branch
carries its dependencies' commits until they merge; review only its own
commits.

Without a caller, #8153, #8155, #8156 and #8157 do not change existing
numerics. Two #8153 changes do apply to every caller, and both keep results
unchanged:

- recomputation through `tensor_parallel.checkpoint` and
  `CheckpointWithoutOutput` restores the forward pass's `contextvars` context
  (`te_checkpoint` is unchanged);
- the router GEMM backward skips gradients nobody requested.

#8152 changes `megatron.rl` import-time behavior (lazy request types, lazy log
file). #7914 is the first PR that wires the feature into a model.
